item.title: Public Hearing on Policy Priorities for Zoning Update
item.description:
Zone In Public Hearing

We’ve begun the work to modernize Columbus’ Zoning Code for the first time in 70 years, but your voice is pivotal in helping us envision how a comprehensive update to our zoning code can support future growth and prosperity, and ultimately shape what our city’s future will look like.

 

We invite you to join us August 21st at Gillie Senior Center for a public hearing hosted by Council President Pro Tem Rob Dorans, Chair of the Building and Zoning Policy Committee, to hear updates on the progress of the Zone In initiative, including identification of policy priorities based on research and community input. Kevin Wheeler, Assistant Director for Growth Policy and Project Manager for Zone In Columbus will present an update and future strategy for this multi-year project.

 

Attendees can attend the hearing via Webex or in person. The hearing will also be broadcast live on CTV, Columbus cable access channel 3, YouTube, and Facebook Live.

 

All interested residents are invited to offer public testimony via WebEx, or in person, during the hearing. Anyone seeking to submit written testimony should forward it to the office of Councilmember Dorans.Written testimony must be received by 3:00pm on the day of the hearing and emailed to Kevin McCain at kbmccain@columbus.gov each speaker's remarks are limited to three minutes or less.

 

Zone In Public Hearing

August 21, 5:00-6:30 PM

Gillie Senior Center

2100 Morse Road

Columbus, Ohio 43229

item.title: Zone In on Community Conversations
Zone In Update: Initial Focus Areas Introduced
item.description:
Zone In Project Update 

WHERE DO WE BEGIN? 

When we started asking folks to tell us about their challenges navigating Columbus’ zoning code, we often got the response, “where do I begin?” We know that a modernized code can help unlock development potential and direct Columbus’ growth toward a more equitable future. But to ensure our work to modernize our code is impactful, we had to ask ourselves, “Where – geographically -- do we begin?”

Today, we’ve issued a report and map that identify initial the focus areas for modernized zoning. Next, we need help from the people who live and work on the corridors to inform how we design the new code, to best accommodate housing, offices, retail and other amenities that meet our current and future needs, values and aspirations.       

       

 

INTERESTED IN LERNING MORE?

Are you interested in hearing more about the report and the status of this project? Joint our project team for a live webinar where we will provide a project overview, discuss the report and hear about ways to get involved in the zoning code update! 

Live Virtual Webinar : Monday April 10 | 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM

Can't make it? A recording of the webinar will be available on our project website! 

 

CHECK OUT OUR NEW WEBSITE! 

Zone In Columbus has a new project website. This site will be updated regularly with project information, interactive maps, and upcoming events!

item.title: Save the Date - Zone In Update
Save the Date - Zone In Update
Zone In on our Future!
item.description:
Zone In on our future!

 

Columbus is growing like never before. By 2050, Central Ohio is expected to grow by 1 million new residents. We know we need to think about things differently – and act now.

 

As Columbus looks forward, we have an opportunity to plan for and guide an equitable, sustainable, and prosperous future for all our residents. One tool to support equitable growth is Columbus’ zoning code. The City of Columbus is embarking on an effort – Zone in Columbus – to modernize our code and better reflect our community’s needs and opportunities for housing, transportation, and equitable development. 

 

The City of Columbus has partnered with the YWCA of Columbus to host Undesign the Redline, an interactive exhibit that explores the history of structural racism through urban planning and its long-term impacts. We invite you to explore this exhibit with your neighbors to learn more about our history, share your own stories, and help us invent a new future for Columbus where all our neighbors, businesses, and communities thrive. We hope you can attend one of the following community events or visit the display for a self-guided tour while it travels through Columbus neighborhoods!
